text:
**Short answer: LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most buyers.** NMC only makes sense if weight is critical or you'll use the unit rarely.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000–6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500–1,000 for NMC. Used daily, that's about 8 years versus under 2 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently when they failed. Peak temperatures were 259°C for LFP versus 731°C for NMC in one study. LFP isn't fireproof, and it didn't tolerate overcharge better in one test, but it's milder when things go wrong ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Price:** One site's data shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC, and LFP is far cheaper per rated cycle ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Availability:** Nearly all current stations are LFP. NMC survives mostly in older or small units.

**Where NMC wins**
- **Energy density:** NMC cells store more per kilogram. But in finished stations the gap shrinks a lot, because the inverter, case and fans weigh the same either way. One database found only about 10% difference in median Wh per pound, and some LFP stations are lighter than some NMC ones ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Compare the actual weight specs.

**What chemistry doesn't decide**
- **Cold weather:** Most stations, both chemistries, won't charge below 32°F. Check the specific model's manual. Some sources claim LFP is much better in the cold, but others found the limits depend more on the maker.
- **Cycle ratings:** Check the end point (80% vs. 70% capacity). A "4,000 cycles to 70%" claim is weaker than "3,000 to 80%."
- **Fit:** Output watts, surge and capacity matter more than chemistry. Size the unit to what you need to run.

**When to choose what**
- **Daily or frequent use (van, off-grid, solar):** LiFePO4.
- **Indoor or in-vehicle storage:** LiFePO4.
- **Rare outages or a few weekends a year:** either works, so choose on price and weight.
- **Already own a working NMC unit:** keep using it.
